content: Deterministic hash splitting hashes a stable identifier (usually query text or sample id) with hashlib.sha256/md5 and maps the digest to a split by a threshold or modulo; identical inputs always land in the same split across runs and machines, and adding new samples does not reshuffle existing assignments. Never use Python's builtin hash(): it is salted per process by PYTHONHASHSEED. For SIF, sha256(normalized query text).digest()[0] < 128 gives a stable 50/50 tuning/held-out split; normalization (NFC + casefold + whitespace collapse) must precede hashing.
